side.name: Homelessness

side.name: High rent
side.line: I pay too much for housing.

why.detail: One is about what I see happening to others and the other is about my own bills, so people can tell them apart at a glance. Homelessness is seeing neighbors with no home; High rent is my own housing costing too much.

why.detail: Fearing I'll lose my own home is a personal pain, while seeing more neighbors with no home is a societal one, and the two are worth linking across pages.

side.name: Don’t know my neighbors
side.line: I don't know the people who live near me.

why.detail: A town can be thriving and still full of strangers, so these are different complaints. Dying town is people and businesses leaving; Neighbors is not knowing the people who are still here.

why.detail: Someone watching their town empty out and someone angry that decisions are made elsewhere would each pick their own without hesitation. Dying town is the place emptying out; Local control is who makes the decisions about it.

side.line: Most days I don't talk to anyone who really knows me.

why.detail: Not knowing neighbors is about the street and the community, while loneliness is a personal feeling that can happen anywhere. Loneliness is feeling alone; Neighbors is not knowing the people on my street, which many people with close friends also feel.

side.name: Distrust
side.line: I can't trust the people around me any more.

side.name: Meanness
side.line: I see people be meaner than they used to.

why.detail: These are close, so the alternative wordings sharpen Trust toward relying on people and Moral decline toward how people treat each other. Trust is whether I can rely on people around me; Moral decline is a sense that people treat each other worse.

side.name: Institutions
side.line: I see the institutions we rely on falling apart.

why.detail: The current Trust line says 'people and groups', which blurs into institutions, so the alternative drops 'groups' and keeps the two distinct. Trust is about the people around me; Institutions is about courts, elections and agencies falling apart.

current.name: Distrust

side.name: Meanness

why.detail: Losing a friend over a disagreement is a specific experience that someone would pick out from a general sense that people are worse. Polarization is losing people when we disagree; Moral decline is people treating each other worse in general.

side.name: Can't share costs
side.line: I know we could afford it together, but there's no way to pool our money.

side.name: Wealth gap
side.line: I see a few people get richer every year while most of us fall further behind.

why.detail: One is a missing tool for people to buy things together and the other is a society-wide gap, so they don't compete for the same pick. Sharing is wanting a way to pool money with others; Inequality is the gap between rich and poor growing.

why.detail: Not being able to get anyone together and being stuck in meetings that go nowhere are different stages of the same effort, and people know which one they're in. Organizing is not getting neighbors to act at all; Meetings is groups that meet but get nothing done.

side.name: Climate change
side.line: I'm worried about the planet heating up.

side.name: Dirty air
side.line: The air where I live isn't clean enough to breathe safely.

why.detail: Someone near a highway or a refinery and someone worried about global heating are naming different things, even when the same fuel causes both. Climate change is the planet heating up over decades; dirty air is what I breathe in my own neighborhood today.

why.detail: A person rebuilding after a flood and a person anxious about the future would each pick one without thinking twice. Disasters are floods, fires, storms and heat I'm living through now; climate change is the worry about where the planet is heading.

side.name: Discrimination against me
side.line: I get treated worse at work, in stores or by landlords because of who I am.

side.name: Prejudice around me
side.line: I see people around me treated badly because of their race, religion, or who they love.

why.detail: Being on the receiving end and being a witness are different places to stand, but with the names "Discrimination" and "Prejudice" people can't tell them apart, so the alternatives sharpen both names. Discrimination is being treated worse myself; prejudice is seeing it happen to other people.

side.name: Prejudice around me
side.line: I see people around me treated badly because of their race, religion, or who they love.

why.detail: Someone angry about sentencing or policing names an institution, while someone bothered by how neighbors or coworkers treat people names something else, so each picks one easily. Justice is unequal treatment by police and courts; prejudice is unequal treatment by people in everyday life.

why.detail: They often travel together, but someone can be bothered by the wealth gap today without naming mobility, and the other way around. Inequality is the gap in money and wealth now; opportunity is whether where you start decides where you end up.
